queer_characters.name: Cheryl
queer_characters.notes: Described as a Black lesbian filmmaker protagonist; a fully realized central character whose life and relationships drive the narrative.

queer_characters.name: Diana
queer_characters.notes: Described as a white lesbian whom Cheryl dates during production.

queer_characters.name: Fae Richards
queer_characters.notes: A fictional 1930s-40s Black lesbian actress whose queerness is uncovered through Cheryl's documentary; framed as recovering an erased queer history.

queer_characters.name: June Walker
queer_characters.notes: Described as a Black woman who was Fae's long-term partner of 20 years; the source states the relationship but does not assign her a specific label.

queer_characters.name: Shirley Hamilton
queer_characters.notes: Described as an older Black lesbian, a friend of Cheryl's mother, offering intergenerational queer presence.

queer_creators.name: Cheryl Dunye
queer_creators.notes: Directed, wrote, edited, and starred in the film; described as the first feature directed by a Black lesbian and stated 'our stories have never been told.'

contributor_notes: The film is a mockumentary blending fiction and documentary, with Dunye playing a version of herself. Fae Richards and June Walker are fictional 1930s-40s figures depicted via staged archival materials, hence historical-context rep_quality. Spicy level defaulted to 1 as the source text does not describe explicit sexual content. No subtitle or audio language info provided. Racism trigger warning drawn from the description of 'mammy' roles Fae was relegated to; a maintainer should verify scope.
